attempted_derivation.blocking_gap: The derivation proves only an upper-bound/falsifier lemma. It does not prove C(H_N)>N^{1+epsilon} for any explicit high-entropy carrier.
steps: Fix N and position i; let R_i be the set of formulas reachable as x varies.

For this position, build a nonuniform evaluator either by hardwiring SAT(y) for every y in R_i and comparing Gamma_{N,i}(x) to the dictionary, or by brute-force checking all 2^{v_i} assignments of the produced formula.
The cheaper evaluator costs min{|R_i|,2^{v_i}} L_N^{O(1)} gates, after Gamma_N has produced the query bits.
Run the batched generator once, evaluate all M_N positioned queries, and OR the M_N answers.
This gives C(H_N)<=N^{rho+o(1)}+N^{q+o(1)}+B_N L_N^{O(1)}; taking the contrapositive yields the entropy threshold gate.
attempted_derivation.why_not_yet_a_proof: Even with q,rho<1+epsilon and theta_N>=1+epsilon, the main missing step is a non-natural general-circuit lower bound for H_N; the bridge is route-level progress, not P != NP.

branch_outputs.branch_title: Hardness-Magnification Bridge Realization: positioned entropy cover gate

assumptions: Circuit size means nonuniform Boolean circuit size over a fixed finite fan-in basis; polylogarithmic factors are absorbed into N^{o(1)}.
For each position i, formulas in R_i use at most v_i Boolean variables; a circuit may either table SAT on R_i or brute-force all 2^{v_i} assignments.
The source lower bound C(H_N)>N^{1+epsilon} is interpreted on the same valid length set as the generator family, either eventually or i.o. with matching quantifiers.
definitions: source object: H_N on N input bits, H_N(x)=OR over M_N=N^{q+o(1)} SAT queries y_i(x)=Gamma_{N,i}(x) of length L_N=(log N)^d and variable count v_i.
target object: SAT notin P/poly, obtained only by substituting hypothetical SAT circuits into all generated queries and contradicting a source lower bound for H_N.
controlled interface: a batched generator Gamma_N of circuit size N^{rho+o(1)} exposes all query positions, with no uncharged advice and with per-position ranges R_i={Gamma_{N,i}(x):x in {0,1}^N}.
target-preserving condition: max{rho,q}<1+epsilon, L_N=(log N)^d with d>1, and every fixed SAT exponent c contributes only L_N^c=N^{o(1)} to the carrier circuit.

attempted_derivation.blocking_gap: No known method proves the required SAT correlation soundness for theta_m<N against SIZE(m^k). Low theta_m is blocked by the natural-proofs falsifier under standard PRF assumptions; high theta_m avoids largeness but demands a much stronger average-case lower bound.
steps: Fix m and N=2^m; encode every m-input Boolean function F as a +/-1 truth table and let T_m be SAT_m.
Define P_theta by the signed correlation inequality <F,T_m> >= theta_m. Completeness is immediate because <T_m,T_m>=N.
For random F, the products F_i T_m(i) are independent Rademacher variables, so the density of P_theta is a one-sided Rademacher tail.
Apply moderate-deviation estimates: theta_m=c sqrt(N log N) yields polynomial density N^{-c^2/2-o(1)}, while theta_m much larger than sqrt(N log N) yields superpolynomially small density.
Membership in P_theta is decidable in poly(N) by computing the SAT_m truth table by brute force and taking an inner product.
If the route proves <T_C,T_m><theta_m for every size m^k circuit C, then P_theta rejects all such circuit truth tables and is useful against SIZE(m^k).
When density is polynomial, the resulting property distinguishes random truth tables from truth tables of size m^k PRFs with advantage delta_m, giving the precise natural-proof obstruction.

When density is superpolynomially small, the natural-proof transfer is invalid; the escape is real only if the route can prove the stronger average-case correlation lower bound without advice leakage.
attempted_derivation.why_not_yet_a_proof: This derivation audits a route-specific bridge and its quantitative barrier threshold. It does not prove SAT lower bounds, P/poly separation, or P != NP.

branch_outputs.branch_title: Barrier-Aware Lower-Bound Route: Correlation Halfspace Gate

assumptions: Boolean functions are represented by +/-1 truth tables of length N=2^m.
SAT_m is explicit enough that its full truth table is computable in poly(N) time.
The route proves the uniform family of inequalities <T_C,T_m> < theta_m for every circuit C of size at most m^k.
The threshold theta_m is the same in the density calculation and in the small-circuit soundness claim.
definitions: source object: For m input bits let N=2^m and T_m in {+/-1}^N be the SAT_m truth table; the certificate is P_theta={F:<F,T_m> >= theta_m} plus soundness for SIZE(m^k).

target object: A Razborov-Rudich natural property over N-bit truth tables, constructible in poly(N), large with density delta_m, useful against m-input circuits of size m^k, and giving a PRF distinguisher of advantage delta_m.
controlled interface: Use only the same halfspace P_theta; compute T_m by exhaustive SAT in poly(N); transfer completeness, soundness, density, and constructivity without claiming P != NP.

target-preserving condition: The threshold satisfies 0 <= theta_m < N and soundness quantifies over every nonuniform circuit of size m^k on m inputs, so an exact small SAT circuit would contradict soundness.

equations.label: correlation_threshold_property
equations.valid_when: Valid when Boolean functions are encoded as +/-1 truth tables and theta_m is below N.

equations.label: density_as_rademacher_tail
equations.valid_when: Valid when T_m is fixed and F is uniformly random over all N-bit truth tables.

equations.label: moderate_deviation_threshold
equations.valid_when: Applies in the moderate-deviation regime c=O(1) with theta_m=o(N).

equations.label: superpolynomial_largeness_loss
equations.valid_when: Valid when theta_m=o(N) and standard Rademacher tail asymptotics remain applicable.

equations.label: usefulness_transfer
equations.valid_when: Requires soundness for all nonuniform size m^k circuits at the identical threshold theta_m.

equations.label: prf_distinguisher_advantage
equations.valid_when: Applies after PRF truth tables have circuit size at most m^k and the property is poly(N)-constructive.

candidate_lemmas.statement: For fixed k, a SAT correlation-halfspace certificate at threshold theta_m transfers to a Razborov-Rudich natural property useful against SIZE(m^k) exactly while the halfspace has polynomial density. Quantitatively, theta_m=c sqrt(N log N) gives density N^{-c^2/2-o(1)}, while theta_m/sqrt(N log N)->infinity loses largeness. Thus a low-correlation global predicate is a valid natural-proof object; a high-correlation predicate is outside this falsifier only by requiring stronger average-case SAT hardness.

assumptions: The transcript tau_m is computable in poly(N), for example by running Pi_m on the explicit SAT_m truth table.
The fiber A_tau is the set of all truth tables inducing exactly tau_m.
The separator has one-sided completeness for SAT_m and universal soundness against SIZE(m^k).

interface: freeze the actual transcript tau_m taken by SAT_m and test membership by rerunning Pi_m and checking tau_m.

attempted_derivation.blocking_gap: No actual sparse non-natural certificate source with proved soundness and a proved tau_V profile is known. The derivation supplies a valid cap and falsifier, not a carrier construction.
steps: Fix a deterministic canonical accepted transcript producing y_m and partition its 2^m output positions into blocks of length 2^{lambda m}.
Hardwire the checkpoint configuration at the start of each block; this costs 2^{(1-lambda+sigma)m+o(m)} gates as constants in a nonuniform circuit for y_m.
On input index i, compute its block and offset, select the hardwired checkpoint, and invoke the source-model block decoder of size 2^{tau_V(lambda)m+o(m)}.
Optimize over lambda to obtain CKT(y_m)<=2^{alpha_V m+o(m)}.
Compare the claimed MCSP no-side threshold epsilon with alpha_V; if epsilon exceeds alpha_V, the accepted transcript contradicts its own soundness.
If the source survives this audit and is kappa-dense with O(m)-bit canonical certificates, apply the existing exhaustive-selection transfer to get E lower bound exponent delta<epsilon/kappa.
attempted_derivation.why_not_yet_a_proof: This is route-level progress only. It can refute overstrong MCSP carrier sources and quantify a valid transfer, but it does not construct high-MCSP truth tables or prove P != NP.

assumptions: Output length is T_m=2^m and the output index is the m-bit input to the extracted Boolean function.
A checkpoint of the selected transcript, including work state, heads, and certificate position, has bit length S_m<=2^{sigma m+o(m)}.
For block length 2^{lambda m}, the selected source model admits nonuniform circuits of size 2^{tau_V(lambda)m+o(m)} that compute the requested within-block output bit from a checkpoint and offset.
The cap is an upper bound on emitted-table circuit complexity; it is not itself a construction of a high-MCSP carrier.
definitions: source object: a deterministic uniform streaming certificate verifier V(1^m,c) with |c|=O(m), canonical acceptance, and output y_m in {0,1}^{2^m} claimed to be on the no-side of MCSP_{m,2^{epsilon m}}.
target object: an E-language L whose length-m truth table is the selected accepted y_m on kappa-dense source lengths, intended to yield L notin SIZE(2^{delta n}).
controlled interface: exhaustive E-time enumeration of O(m)-bit certificates, hardwired checkpoints from the selected transcript, and a named within-block decoder circuit family for V.
target-preserving condition: the transfer preserves threshold epsilon, density kappa, uniform canonical selection, and excludes advice, hidden randomness, and nonuniform witness-location leakage.

equations.valid_when: Valid when the whole selected verifier configuration is explicitly bounded in bits.

equations.label: block_storage_cost
equations.valid_when: Valid when checkpoints are hardwired at every block boundary of one accepted transcript.

equations.label: within_block_decoder
equations.valid_when: Valid when the source model supplies the named block-decoding simulation bound.

equations.label: checkpoint_cap
equations.valid_when: Applies after storage and within-block decoding are combined in one circuit.

equations.valid_when: Valid when lambda ranges over exponential block lengths inside the truth table.

candidate_lemmas.failure_test: If a proposed source asserts threshold epsilon>alpha_V, its accepted output has small circuits from checkpoints, so the MCSP no-side certificate is unsound.
candidate_lemmas.proof_role: Route obstruction and repair lemma. It replaces the earlier single exponent (1+sigma)/2 by a source-model parameter tau_V, making the checkpoint argument valid only after block simulation is named.
candidate_lemmas.statement: A sequential MCSP carrier has a model-sensitive checkpoint cap. If V has checkpoint size S_m<=2^{sigma m+o(m)} and within-block decoder exponent tau_V(lambda), then every accepted emitted truth table has circuit size at most 2^{alpha_V m+o(m)}, where alpha_V=inf_lambda max(1-lambda+sigma,tau_V(lambda)). Thus a claimed no-side threshold 2^{epsilon m} is valid only when epsilon<=alpha_V; epsilon>alpha_V is a falsifier for source soundness.

assumptions: 0<=sigma<=1 for the displayed ideal-local equality.
The emitted table is fixed by one canonical certificate; otherwise checkpoint constants encode nonuniform witness choices.
The circuit upper bound is nonuniform, which is sufficient to refute MCSP no-side soundness.
definitions: Locally block-simulable means that advancing 2^{lambda m} sequential steps from a checkpoint costs 2^{lambda m+o(m)} circuit gates for the requested output bit.
Full-configuration simulation means each step may require manipulating an S_m-bit configuration representation, giving tau_V(lambda)=lambda+sigma up to lower-order terms.
The threshold audit compares epsilon with the appropriate alpha_V, not with a folklore checkpoint exponent.

equations.label: ideal_local_cap
equations.valid_when: Valid when the verifier has a true local block decoder of linear block cost.

equations.label: full_configuration_cap
equations.valid_when: Valid when each simulated step may touch an explicit exponential-size configuration.

candidate_lemmas.failure_test: A proof that cites (1+sigma)/2 without proving tau_V(lambda)=lambda is invalid for this route.
candidate_lemmas.proof_role: Model-separation lemma for the source side. It prevents importing the stronger local cap into a random-access or full-state verifier model.
candidate_lemmas.statement: In the ideal locally block-simulable streaming model, tau_V(lambda)=lambda+o(1), so alpha_V=(1+sigma)/2 for 0<=sigma<=1. In a full-configuration RAM simulation with tau_V(lambda)=lambda+sigma, the cap weakens to alpha_V=1/2+sigma. Therefore the source model must be declared before using the checkpoint exponent.

assumptions: Certificate length is O(m), verifier time is 2^{O(m)}, and the selected table is computable by exhaustive search in E time.
Soundness means every accepted y_m has circuit complexity greater than 2^{epsilon m}.
The padding map preserves uniformity and increases input length by at most a factor kappa.
definitions: A kappa-dense source has a valid carrier length m in every interval [n,kappa n] for all sufficiently large n.
Canonical selection chooses the lexicographically first accepting O(m)-bit certificate and emitted table, eliminating nonuniform leakage.
The E-language pads missing lengths by the nearest later carrier length inside the kappa window.

candidate_lemmas.proof_role: Target-preserving extraction theorem with a new quantitative ceiling from L18.1.
candidate_lemmas.statement: If a kappa-dense, uniform, canonical MCSP carrier source is sound at threshold 2^{epsilon m} and passes the cap audit epsilon<=alpha_V, then exhaustive selection defines an E-language with circuit lower bound exponent every delta<epsilon/kappa. If epsilon>alpha_V, or if selection uses advice, the target-preserving transfer fails.

assumptions: The barrier audit concerns largeness of the property, not the truth of P != NP.
